items.title: Move the report, keep its clause

states.label: Knowing now
states.sm: ʻUa iloa e le tama ʻua sau le teine.
states.en: The boy knows that the girl has come.
states.note: The coming is already done at the time of the knowing.

states.label: Knowing then
states.sm: Na iloa e le tama ʻua sau le teine.
states.en: The boy knew that the girl had come.
states.note: The report is in the past. The coming was already done then, and its Samoan particle has not moved.

items.caption: The first tense particle changes. The reported clause stays word for word the same, while English changes has come to had come.

items.title: Staying at the time of the report

states.label: Report at now
states.sm: ʻUa iloa e le tama ʻoloʻo nofo le teine ʻi le nuʻu.
states.en: The boy knows that the girl is staying in the village.

states.label: Report in the past
states.sm: Na iloa e le tama ʻoloʻo nofo le teine ʻi le nuʻu.
states.en: The boy knew that the girl was staying in the village.

items.caption: The happening-now particle inside the report places the staying at the same time as the knowing, whether that knowing is now or in the past.

items.title: What is being passed on?

data.question: What kind of report is this?

prompts.sm: Na iloa e le tama ʻua sasae le ʻie.
prompts.why: A knowing word is followed by an ordinary clause with its own tense particle.

prompts.sm: ʻUa faʻatonu mai e le teine o le vaʻalele ʻia nofo le tagata.
prompts.why: The mood particle *ʻia* opens the reported command.

prompts.sm: Na fai mai le teine pē nofo le tama ʻi le nuʻu.
prompts.why: *Pē* opens the reported question after the say-verb.

items.intro: Read how the reported part begins and choose what is being reported.
